verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: Then the Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary:
13:1 "Then the word of the Lord came to me saying" This chapter is an amplification
of Ezek. 12:24, dealing with "false" prophets.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要说预言攻击以色列中说预言的先知，对那些本己心发预言的说：『你们当听耶和华的话。』」
verses.en: “Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are now prophesying. Say to the prophets who prophesy from their imagination:[NOTE:1] ‘Listen to the Lord’s message!
notes: Heb “from their mind.” sn Who prophesy from their imagination. Note the testimony of Moses in Num 16:28, which contains a similar expression.
verses.commentary:
13:2 "prophesy against the prophets of Israel" Another category of Judean society is condemned! There are
six charges brought against these prophets.

- they prophesied from their own inspiration

- they followed their own spirit

- they have seen nothing

- they have not gone into the breaches for My people

- they see falsehood

- they have misled My people

The question, "How do you know a false prophet?" is extremely important (see full notes on the following texts online,
Deut. 13:1-5; 18:21-22; Matt. 7; 1 John 4:1-3). This passage in Ezekiel is reminiscent of Jeremiah, chapters 23; 28; 29.

The VERB "prophesy" (BDB 612, KB 659) is used twice in this verse.

- Niphal IMPERATIVE

- Niphal PARTICIPLE

The NOUN "prophets" (nabi, BDB 611) is also used. See Special Topic following.

A good discussion of the characteristics of false prophets is found in The Hermeneutical Spiral by Grant R. Osborne, pp. 210-211.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT), I. B.

▣ "who prophesy from their own inspiration" See 2 Pet. 2:1-3 description of false prophets. The Hebrew
term behind "inspiration" is "hearts" (BDB 524).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "'Listen to the word of the Lord'" The VERB "listen" is literally "hear"
(BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE). YHWH is addressing the false prophets. This is a common VERB
in the prophets. Notice a sample of who/what is addressed.

- Ezek. 3:17 ‒ Ezekiel

- Ezek. 6:3; 36:1,4 ‒ the mountains of Israel

- Ezek. 13:2 ‒ false prophets

- Ezek. 16:35 ‒ harlot

- Ezek. 18:25; 33:7,30 ‒ house of Israel

- Ezek. 20:47 ‒ forest of the Negev

- Ezek. 25:3 ‒ sons of Ammon

- Ezek. 34:7,9 ‒ shepherds (i.e. leaders)

- Ezek. 37:4 ‒ the dry bones

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema), I. B.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「愚顽的先知有祸了，他们随从自己的心意，却一无所见。
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit but have seen nothing!
verses.commentary:
13:3 "the Lord God" This title is a combination of the terms

- Adon ‒ BDB 10 (SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD [adon and kurios])

- YHWH ‒ BDB 217 (SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)

▣ "'Woe'" This is the literary marker (BDB 222) for a prophetic literary form known as a funeral dirge.
It is common in Isaiah (e.g. Isa. 5:8,11,18, 20, 21,22) and Jeremiah (e.g. Jer. 22:13,18 [four times]),
but found in Ezekiel only in Ezek. 13:3,18 and 34:2.

Several of the chapters in Isaiah begin with "Woe" (cf. Isaiah 28; 29; 30; 31; 33).

▣ "foolish prophets" This seems to refer to self deception (cf. Jer. 23:21-22), not low intelligence.
The ADJECTIVE (BDB 614, KB 663 II) is used to describe Israel in Deut. 32:6,21.

There is a Hebrew word play between

- prophet ‒ נביאום

- foolish ‒ נבלום

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOLISH, #3

▣ "who are following their own spirit" Here is the problem! It is their own spirit that is leading them,
not God's Spirit! They speak their word in God's name!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

verses.zh: 以色列啊，你的先知好像荒场中的狐狸，
verses.en: Your prophets have become like jackals among the ruins, O Israel.
verses.commentary:
13:4 "your prophets have been like foxes among ruins" Their only concern was for themselves (Ezek. 13:5).
The word "foxes" (BDB 1043) may be a theological wordplay on

- "ruins" (BDB 352) ‒ places where foxes live (i.e. Jerusalem will be a place of ruins)

- "foxes" ‒ some desert animals that lived in the ruins of destroyed cities became associated
with the demonic (NEB)

- "foxes" ‒ this term may also imply that these false prophets fed on the people
(cf. Ps. 63:10)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEMONIC IN THE OT, B. #6

verses.zh: 没有上去堵挡破口，也没有为以色列家重修墙垣，使他们当耶和华的日子在阵上站立得住。
verses.en: You have not gone up in the breaks in the wall, nor repaired a wall for the house of Israel that it would stand strong in the battle on the day of the Lord.
verses.commentary:
13:5 This verse uses siege imagery to describe the false prophets' lack of action on behalf of the covenant people.

- did not go into the breaches ‒ BDB 829, "breaches" were holes made in the walls of cities
by the enemy (cf. Isa. 58:12; Amos 4:3; 9:11)

- did not fortify the wall ‒ BDB 154, a good parallel to both images is Ezek. 22:30

Israel's only hope is in their God. These false religionists do not know Him.

▣ "the day of the Lord" This is imagery for the coming of YHWH's
personal presence (cf. Ezek. 7:10,19; 30:3; Isa. 2:2; 13:6,9; 22:5; 34:8; Jer. 46:10; Joel 1:15; 2:1,11,31; 3:14;
Amos 5:18,20; Zeph. 1:7,14; Zech. 14:1; Mal. 4:5). Israel often expected it to be a day of blessing and
affirmation, but here it was a day of judgment. Judah was not in compliance with the Mosaic Covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DAY OF THE LORD (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

verses.zh: 这些人所见的是虚假，是谎诈的占卜。他们说是耶和华说的，其实耶和华并没有差遣他们，他们倒使人指望那话必然立定。
verses.en: They see delusion and their omens are a lie.[NOTE:1] They say, “The Lord declares,” though the Lord has not sent them;[NOTE:2] yet they expect their word to be confirmed.[NOTE:3]
notes: The same description of a false prophet is found in Micah 2:11.
The Lord has not sent them. A similar concept is found in Jer 14:14 and 23:21.
Or “confirmed”; NIV11 has “to fulfill,” TEV “to come true.”
verses.commentary:
13:6-7 These false prophets are characterized by several terms.

- they see falsehood (literally "vanity" or "nothingness," BDB 996;
see SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS

- they see lying divination (BDB 890 construct 469;
see SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION), cf. Ezek. 22:28; Micah 2:11

- the Lord has not sent them (BDB 1018, KB 1511, Qal PERFECT, cf. Jer. 14:14; 23:21)

- their message is not from YHWH, Ezek. 13:7 (BDB 180, KB 210, Piel PERFECT)

They claim to be YHWH's representatives, but they knowingly speak their own messages (cf. Ezek. 13:6c). These
false prophets/preachers/teachers are always a problem for the people of God, Old Testament and New Testament.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FALSE TEACHERS

▣ "the Lord declares" This is exactly the prophetic formula that
Ezekiel and Jeremiah used. It was so difficult to know who was/is from God and who was/is not
(cf. Jeremiah 28-29). See the important note at Ezek. 13:2.

verses.zh: 你们岂不是见了虚假的异象吗？岂不是说了谎诈的占卜吗？你们说，这是耶和华说的，其实我没有说。」
verses.en: Have you not seen a false vision and announced a lying omen when you say, “The Lord declares,” although I myself never spoke?

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：「因你们说的是虚假，见的是谎诈，我就与你们反对。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: “‘Therefore, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because you have spoken false words and forecast delusion, look,[NOTE:1] I am against you,[NOTE:2] declares the Sovereign Lord.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.

Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘hinnenî ’êlékâ’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.

verses.zh: 我的手必攻击那见虚假异象、用谎诈占卜的先知，他们必不列在我百姓的会中，不录在以色列家的册上，也不进入以色列地；你们就知道我是主耶和华。
verses.en: My hand will be against the prophets who see delusion and announce lying omens. They will not be included in the council[NOTE:1] of my people, nor be written in the registry[NOTE:2] of the house of Israel, nor enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Sovereign Lord.
notes: The Hebrew term may refer to the secret council of the Lord (Jer 23:18; Job 15:8), but here it more likely refers to a human council comprised of civic leaders (Gen 49:6; Jer 6:11; 15:17; Pss 64:3; 111:1).

The reference here is probably to a civil list (as in Ezra 2:16; Neh 7:64) rather than to a “book of life” (Exod 32:32; Isa 4:3; Ps 69:29; Dan 12:1). This registry may have been established at the making of David’s census (2 Sam 24:2, 9).
verses.commentary:
13:9 "My hand is against the prophets who see false visions and utter lying divinations" There are three
things God says He will do to these false prophets.

- they will lose their leadership ("council of My people," cf. Ps. 111:1)

- their names will be taken out of the register of the people of God (cf. Ps. 87:6; similar to the lists referred to in Neh. 7:64)

- they will not enter the Promised Land (this message is addressed to false prophets in both
Babylon and Judah).

They are completely removed from God's people!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

verses.zh: 因为他们诱惑我的百姓，说：『平安！』其实没有平安，就像有人立起墙壁，他们倒用未泡透的灰抹上。
verses.en: “‘This is because they have led my people astray saying, “All is well,”[NOTE:1] when things are not well. When anyone builds a wall without mortar,[NOTE:2] they coat it with whitewash.
notes: Or “peace.”

The Hebrew word only occurs here in the Bible. According to L. C. Allen (Ezekiel [WBC], 1:202-3), it is also used in the Mishnah of a wall of rough stones without mortar. This fits the context here, which compares the false prophetic messages to a nice coat of whitewash on a structurally unstable wall.
verses.commentary:
13:10

NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB, JPSOA
"they have misled My people"

NKJV
"because they have seduced

My people"

TEV
"the prophets misled My

people"

Peshitta
"they have deceived My

people"

NET
"they had led My people

astray"

LXX
"caused my people to err"

The VERB (BDB 380, KB 377, Hiphil PERFECT) is found only here in the prophets.
It occurs only one other time in Song of Songs 1:7, where it is translated "veils," NASB; "wanders," REV.

- In Arabic the root means "to exceed a just limit" or "one who deviates from the right path."

- In Ethiopian it means "apostasy," "superstition," or "idolatry."

It seems that the term is used of not following the right path or way. YHWH's word was seen as a clearly marked path/road
(cf. Ps. 89:15; 119:105; Prov. 6:2; Isa. 2:5; 1 John 1:6-7). To deviate from this path was to knowingly violate YHWH's covenant (e.g. Job 6:18;
Ps. 16:11; 17:4; 25:4,10; Prov. 2:8,13,19,20; 3:6; 4:18; Isa. 2:3; 3:12). The prophets are willfully self-deluded and leading others astray also.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "saying 'Peace' when there is no peace" This was the problem of the false prophets (cf. Ezek. 13:16).
They were preaching the destruction of Neo-Babylon and the restoration of Israel (possibly following Isaiah's insistence that Jerusalem
would not fall, but things had changed, the covenant promises were conditional on covenant obedience). The prophets Ezekiel and
Jeremiah were prophesying judgment and destruction (cf. Jer. 8:18; 28-29), not peace and safety!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

▣ "a wall" This is a rare term (BDB 300) used only here in the OT. Kimchi (a Jewish commentator of the Middle Ages)
says it means "an inferior partition." It is used in the sense of pretending to build something strong, but which is really very weak (i.e. Neh. 4:3).
Here, it is used symbolically for the theological pronouncements of these false prophets.

▣ "they plastered over the whitewash" They hid their false religious pronouncements with a thin coating of religious language
(cf. Ezek. 13:11)! There may be a wordplay between "plaster" (תפל, BDB 1074 II) and "tasteless" or "unsatisfying prophecies"
(תפל, BDB 1074 II, cf. Lam. 2:14).

verses.zh: 所以你要对那些抹上未泡透灰的人说：『墙要倒塌，必有暴雨漫过。大冰雹啊，你们要降下，狂风也要吹裂这墙。』
verses.en: Tell the ones who coat it with whitewash that it will fall. When there is a deluge of rain, hailstones[NOTE:1] will fall and a violent wind will break out.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and you, O hailstones.”
A violent wind will break out. God’s judgments are frequently described in storm imagery (Pss 18:7-15; 77:17-18; 83:15; Isa 28:17; 30:30; Jer 23:19; 30:23).
verses.commentary:
13:11 YHWH will expose the weakness of their false prophecies (cf. Ezek. 38:22) using imagery from nature.

- flooding rain, Ezek. 13:13

- hailstones, Ezek. 13:13

- a violent wind, Ezek. 13:13

Against these three the true nature of the wall (i.e. prophecies) of these false prophets will be clearly revealed (i.e. "fall,"
BDB 656, KB 709, Qal IMPERFECT, twice in Ezek. 13:11 and the Qal PERFECT in Ezek. 13:12).

In the MT these three natural occurrences are not grammatically parallel, but from the context they are.

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"and you"

NRSV, NJB
——

TEV, REB
"I will send"

LXX
"I will give"

Peshitta
"I will bring"

Vulgate
"I will make"

The MT has "and you" (ואתנה, BDB 61) but BDB suggests an alternate vocalization (cf. Gen. 31:6;
Ezek. 13:11,20; 34:17). The UBS Text Project, p. 36, gives "and you" a "C" rating (considerable doubt) and suggests the translation, "as for you (O stones)." This is either:

- the personification of the hailstone judgment

- an affirmation that YHWH is the direct cause of weather judgment(s), cf. Isa. 28:2; 30:30

verses.zh: 这墙倒塌之后，人岂不问你们说：『你们抹上未泡透的灰在哪里呢？』」
verses.en: When the wall has collapsed, people will ask you, “Where is the whitewash you coated it with?”

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：「我要发怒，使狂风吹裂这墙，在怒中使暴雨漫过，又发怒降下大冰雹，毁灭这墙。
verses.en: “‘Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: In my rage I will make a violent wind break out. In my anger there will be a deluge of rain and hailstones in destructive fury.
verses.commentary:
13:13 "in My wrath. . .in wrath" Wrath (BDB 404, cf. Ezek. 13:15) is anthropomorphic language.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

verses.zh: 我要这样拆毁你们那未泡透灰所抹的墙，拆平到地，以致根基露出，墙必倒塌，你们也必在其中灭亡；你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will break down the wall you coated with whitewash and knock it to the ground so that its foundation is exposed. When it falls you will be destroyed beneath it,[NOTE:1] and you will know that I am the Lord.
notes: Or “within it,” referring to the city of Jerusalem.
verses.commentary:
13:14 "its foundation is laid bare" This is an idiom of total destruction (cf. Micah 1:6 and possibly Hab. 3:13). The VERB
is a Niphal PERFECT (BDB 162, KB 191). The term in the Niphal is often used of nakedness (cf. Ezek. 16:36; 23:29).
YHWH will show the true nature of the false prophets' (male and female) messages of hope and security.

verses.zh: 我要这样向墙和用未泡透灰抹墙的人成就我怒中所定的，并要对你们说：『墙和抹墙的人都没有了。』
verses.en: I will vent my rage against the wall and against those who coated it with whitewash. Then I will say to you, “The wall is no more and those who whitewashed it are no more—
verses.commentary:
13:15 This is a proverb that YHWH directs to these false prophets. All of their efforts and words will come to naught. No lasting results!
Their words and they themselves are no more!

verses.zh: 这抹墙的就是以色列的先知，他们指着耶路撒冷说预言，为这城见了平安的异象，其实没有平安。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: those prophets of Israel who would prophesy about Jerusalem[NOTE:1] and would see visions of peace for it, when there was no peace,” declares the Sovereign Lord.’
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
13:16 "peace" The term "peace" (BDB 1022; see note at v. 10) is used in two senses in this verse.

- The false teachers used it in the sense of the political autonomy of Judah.

- Ezekiel uses it in the sense of a restored relationship with YHWH.

Judah will fall and become a vassal nation to Neo-Babylon, but the exiles who trust and obey will be restored (i.e. in their heart and one day to their land)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT, shalom)

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要面向本民中、从己心发预言的女子说预言，攻击她们，
verses.en: “As for you, son of man, turn toward[NOTE:1] the daughters of your people who are prophesying from their imagination.[NOTE:2] Prophesy against them
notes: Heb “set your face against.”
Heb “from their heart.”
verses.commentary:
13:17 "set your face against" The VERB (BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used
here in the sense of "direct your intention against" (i.e. Ezek. 6:2; 14:8; 15:7; 21:2; 29:2; 35:2; Lev. 20:5; Jer. 21:10; 44:11). The face symbolized
the person and thereby one's personal attention to someone or some thing.

YHWH repeats His opposition to these false prophets (men and women) by using the phrase "prophesy against them" (BDB 612,
KB 659, Niphal IMPERATIVE) at the end of Ezek. 13:17!

▣ "the daughters of your people who are prophesying from their own inspiration" Apparently, along with the false prophets, there
were false prophetesses (cf. Ezek. 13:23). Women active in God's service was/is not an unusual thing. However, as there are false prophets, there
are also false prophetesses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

verses.zh: 说主耶和华如此说：『这些妇女有祸了！她们为众人的膀臂缝靠枕，给高矮之人做下垂的头巾，为要猎取人的性命。难道你们要猎取我百姓的性命，为利己将人救活吗？
verses.en: and say ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Woe to those who sew bands[NOTE:1] on all their wrists[NOTE:2] and make headbands[NOTE:3] for heads of every size to entrap people’s lives![NOTE:4] Will you entrap my people’s lives, yet preserve your own lives?
notes: The wristbands mentioned here probably represented magic bands or charms. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:413.
Heb “joints of the hands.” This may include the elbow and shoulder joints.

The Hebrew term occurs in the Bible only here and in v. 21. It has also been understood as a veil or type of head covering. D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:414) suggests that given the context of magical devices, the expected parallel to the magical arm bands, and the meaning of this Hebrew root (סָפַח [safakh, “to attach” or “join”]), it may refer to headbands or necklaces on which magical amulets were worn.
Heb “human lives” or “souls” (three times in v. 18 and twice in v. 19).
verses.commentary:
13:18 "sew magic bands on all their wrists" This group is seen more like sorceresses (see note online at Deut. 18:10-11) than
prophetesses. The word "magic band" (BDB 492) is found only here (vv. 18, 20) in the OT and has been interpreted several ways.

- as amulets

- as phylacteries (Origen's Hexapla; see SPECIAL TOPIC: PHYLACTERIES)

- as pillows (LXX, JPSOA, KJV)

- bands that bind another person's will (Akkadian root)

The phrase "on all their wrists" is literally "all joints of the hands" (BDB 69 CONSTRUCT BDB 388). This seems
to be similar to modern voodoo with its spells and incantations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "make veils for the heads of persons of every stature" The NOUN
"veils" (BDB 705) appears only here and in Ezek. 13:21 in the OT, possibly from Akkadian root, "to loosen."
KB (607) calls it a robe of coarse material, while LXX has "scarf," or "head covering." Whatever these items were, they were attempts
to control the destinies of people (both negatively as curses and positively as charms, cf. Ezek. 13:19). This is the essence of divination
and the occult. It is an expression of egocentric, superstitious, fallen humanity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: VEIL, SHAWL, COVERING

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

▣ "but preserve the lives of others for yourselves" This shows that whatever their occultic practices were, they were
done for self interest! These false prophets/prophetesses wanted to destroy some people and protect others, but not for the glory of YHWH
rather for their own selfish, manipulative purposes! Religion can be self-deceptive, superstitious, and destructive!

verses.zh: 你们为两把大麦，为几块饼，在我民中亵渎我，对肯听谎言的民说谎，杀死不该死的人，救活不该活的人。』」
verses.en: You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and scraps of bread. You have put to death people[NOTE:1] who should not die and kept alive those who should not live by your lies to my people, who listen to lies!
notes: Heb “human lives” or “souls.”
verses.commentary:
13:19 "for a handful of barley and fragments of bread" It seems improbable that this refers to the payment that these false prophetesses
will receive because it is so meager. However, this phrase is very ambiguous because of the rarity of the words "handful" (BDB 1043) and "fragments"
(BDB 837). In Anatolia and later in Syria handfuls of barley and bread were used as a means of divination and this seems to be the possible historical allusion.

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：「看哪，我与你们的靠枕反对，就是你们用以猎取人、使人的性命如鸟飞的。我要将靠枕从你们的膀臂上扯去，释放你们猎取如鸟飞的人。
verses.en: “‘Therefore, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Take note[NOTE:1] that I am against your wristbands with which you entrap people’s lives[NOTE:2] like birds. I will tear them from your arms and will release the people’s lives, which you hunt like birds.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
Heb “human lives” or “souls.”
verses.commentary:
13:20-21 YHWH will destroy these false spiritualists! He will free their deluded followers!

▣

NASB, REB
"magic bands"

NRSV
"bands"

NKJV
"magic charms"

NJB
"ribbons"

TEV, NET
"wristbands"

Peshitta
"embroidered garments"

LXX
"cushions"

JPSOA
"pads"

The MT has "band" or "fillet" (BDB 492). KB 491 suggests it is from an Akkadian root meaning "to bind one's hands"
for magic purposes. This fits the context best.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "birds" The term (BDB 827 III) occurs twice. It is translated "birds" or "flying things" because of the context of "hunt"
(BDB 844, KB 1010, Polel PARTICIPLE, twice). However, the term normally means

- "to break out" (BDB 827 II, like leprosy, cf. Lev. 13:39)

- "to bud" or "to sprout" (BDB 827 I, cf. Exod. 25:31-34; 37:17-20; Isa. 18:5)

This passage is the only place in the OT that the translation "birds" is used. Because of the occultic context it may refer to giving
people diseases by means of incantations! See the TEV translation, "I hate the wristbands that you use in your attempt to control life and death. I
will rip them off your arms and set free the people that you were controlling."

verses.zh: 我也必撕裂你们下垂的头巾，救我百姓脱离你们的手，不再被猎取，落在你们手中。你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will tear off your headbands and rescue my people from your power;[NOTE:1] they will no longer be prey in your hands. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “from your hand(s).” This refers to their power over the people.

verses.zh: 我不使义人伤心，你们却以谎话使他伤心，又坚固恶人的手，使他不回头离开恶道得以救活。
verses.en: This is because you have disheartened the righteous person with lies (although I have not grieved him), and because you have encouraged the wicked person not to turn from his evil conduct and preserve his life.
verses.commentary:
13:22 This verse assumes that the superstition or magic had some psychological effect!

The VERBAL "disheartened" (BDB 456, KB 454, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is
found only here in this form. Many (KB 454) have assumed it could be a Hiphil PERFECT of a similar root meaning "to cause pain."

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why were the Jewish people (who had the OT) so reluctant to hear the voice of God?

- What is divination?

- Did the lying false prophets know they were false prophets?

- Does God speak through women?

verses.zh: 你们就不再见虚假的异象，也不再行占卜的事；我必救我的百姓脱离你们的手；你们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: Therefore you will no longer see false visions and practice divination. I will rescue my people from your power, and you[NOTE:1] will know that I am the Lord.’”
notes: The Hebrew verb is feminine plural, indicating that it is the false prophetesses who are addressed here.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 13:1-7

1Then the word of the Lord came to me saying, 2"Son of
man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy, and say to those who prophesy from their own inspiration, 'Listen to the word of the Lord!
3Thus says the Lord God, "Woe to the foolish prophets who are following their own spirit and have seen nothing. 4O Israel,
your prophets have been like foxes among ruins. 5You have not gone up into the breaches, nor did you build the wall around the house of Israel to stand in the battle
on the day of the Lord. 6They see falsehood and lying divination who are saying, 'The Lord declares,'
when the Lord has not sent them; yet they hope for the fulfillment of their word. 7Did you not see a false vision and speak a lying
divination when you said, 'The Lord declares,' but it is not I who have spoken?"'"
